::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 2nd 1861  
**From:** Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Westcountry Studies Library, Exeter/ 1861/1
:::

My dear [Miss Smith](people/person_263.qmd)

I did not write yesterday because the parcel was not come, but it is here all safe this morning though I can only testify to the beautiful clear MS as yet. It was rather over weight, which perhaps was the reason of the delay. I think it is possible this may account for the lamented loss of the [Wynnes](other_books/otherbook_267.qmd), as the post will not convey things beyond a certain amount overweight. I once nearly lost all the [Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd) proofs that way, the stamp having fallen off, but luckily there was a direction inside, so they wrote to me and I redeemed it. I have sent your first two chapters to Derby to be printed, though I don’t much think there will be space in April, as the [Easter story](other_books/otherbook_300.qmd) must come in then It was that sent me by [Mrs Carr](people/person_259.qmd) about whom you wrote to me, and whose [friend](people/person_1259.qmd) seems to be a mine of Russian curiosities. Do you know anything about evening sewing classes - a lady wants counsel in the notices to correspondents in the M P upon setting one up, and as I know nothing myself, I shall be grateful for any experience you can give or direct me to. I sent [Aggesden](other_books/otherbook_268.qmd) to a friend in America who likes it very much as also the Wynnes.

yours sincerely

C M Yonge

---

**Note:** Envelope addressed to Miss Ann (paper torn)/ Rectory/ Old Charlton/ SE and postmarked Winchester and London SE 4 March 1861.
